The antidiesel solenoid controls the throttle opening at engine idle to prevent dieseling, which is particularly important in newer emission-controlled vehicles due to higher operating temperatures and other factors. When the ignition switch is turned off, the solenoid deenergizes and the throttle closes tightly, cutting off the air-fuel mixture and preventing the engine from continuing to run [2].

A diesel governor can be actuated through the movement of centrifugal flyweights or by the air-pressure differential produced by a governor valve and venturi assembly. [3] Additionally, it is driven by engine speed in the case of a centrifugal unit that controls another part of the governor system based on the engine's rotational speed. [5]

A battery case is made of hard rubber or polypropylene plastic. This material choice ensures resistance to acid and mechanical shock [1].

Once a battery's electrolyte has been diluted, it will be marked with a special tag indicating the full-charge specific gravity. Additionally, a 1-inch white spot will be painted on the battery top [2].

A typical vibrating current regulator consists of a soft iron core, a heavy winding or current coil around the core, a set of regulator contact points normally held closed by spring tension, and a resistance unit connected across the two regulator contact points [1].

The regulator stops the generator from exceeding its rated output by cutting a resistance intermittently into and out of the shunt-field circuit as the regulator contact points open and close due to varying magnetic pull. This action regulates the current flow, preventing it from surpassing the maximum set for the generator [1]. Additionally, in voltage regulation mode, the voltage coil connected across the generator brushes and parallel with the battery senses the output voltage and adjusts accordingly to maintain a constant voltage regardless of speed or load conditions [3].

The no-charge warning lamp knows that the alternator has stopped charging because when the alternator stops producing sufficient current, the magnetic coil of the field relay is not energized by the stator windings. This causes the contact points to remain open, allowing current from the battery to pass through a series-parallel arrangement including an indicator lamp and a resistor. As a result, the indicator lamp lights up when there is no charge being produced by the alternator [2][3].

Adding a capacitor makes the test lamp flash brighter when the points open because the capacitor speeds up the magnetic collapse, causing faster-moving lines across the secondary winding. This results in higher voltage and more current, leading to a brighter light. [1]

Blackout lighting is designed to provide the vehicle operator with sufficient light to operate the vehicle in total darkness and to show vehicle position to a leading or trailing vehicle when illumination must be restricted to a level not visible to a distant enemy. [2]

According to excerpt [5], the magnetic fuel gauge is self-regulating and requires no voltage-limiting devices because variations in electrical system voltage will affect both magnetic coils equally, thus not upsetting the differential created between them. Therefore, it inherently does not require a separate voltage regulator.

The contact angle of a flat thrust bearing is 90 degrees. This information is cited from [1].
A double-row angular-contact bearing provides rigid lengthwise support in both directions, whereas a single-row angular-contact bearing only supports in one direction. This is stated in [2].

On a fully floating axle, the axle shafts transmit only turning effort or torque and do not bear any other forces such as the weight of the differential or stresses caused by wheel movement. The stresses from turning, skidding, and wobbling are taken entirely by the axle housing through the wheel bearings [3].

The ultimate limit to how hard a vehicle can be slowed is determined by the coefficient of friction between the tire and the road, as well as the risk of locking the wheels which would lead to skidding rather than controlled braking. Maximum retardation is achieved when the wheel is about to lock, at this point, the friction between brake surfaces is almost equal to that between the tire and road [1]. This indicates that beyond this point, further increase in braking force could cause loss of control due to reduced traction from sliding tires instead of effective braking action.

In an air-over-hydraulic brake system, air pressure is used to operate a master cylinder which then functions similarly to those in hydraulic systems by converting fluid pressure into mechanical force that pushes the brake shoes against the drums. The key difference lies in the initial actuation method where air pressure operates the system rather than direct hydraulic pressure [3]. In contrast, in a purely hydraulic system, fluid pressure directly moves the pistons within wheel cylinders which push the brake shoes outward against the brake drum [1].

The side rails of truck frames follow standardized SAE (Society of Automotive Engineers) widths to permit the mounting of stock transmissions, transfer assemblies, rear axles, and similar components [1].

The frames of trucks that are used as prime movers are built heavier, particularly with additional reinforcement of the side rails and rear crossmembers. This design compensates for the added towing stresses encountered when these vehicles are used to tow other equipment or trailers [1].

The PSB system uses a plunger-type pump that creates high-pressure fuel charges for the injectors. This pump is driven by a camshaft and is compact and self-contained, housing all components of the injectors.
